title: progressive-traffic-guardrail-playbook-and-operator-canvas
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a pragmatic operator-centered UX for progressive traffic control, canary/A-B experiments, and automated fallback policies. Goal is to produce a small set of wireframe annotations and a prioritized backlog so engineering can start a thin vertical: configure -> preview -> apply -> monitor -> rollback.

Context / motivation:
- Customers routinely need to test new model variants (quantized vs fp16, different model families) with minimal blast radius.
- Operators are often product engineers or SREs who want predictable defaults but the ability to tweak.
- Existing console flows focus on single-step deployments; we need explicit orchestration for progressive release + safety autopilot.

Primary personas:
- Platform operator (Sam): wants default safe options, quick canaries, and a clear audit trail.
- Feature owner (Priya): wants to run A/B experiments with metrics and bucketing for feature evaluation.
- SRE (Diego): wants rollback, circuit-breaker controls, and latency/cost guardrails.

High-level requirements (UX implications):
1) Fast path: create a rollout in < 3 clicks with sane defaults (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%, 10m evaluation windows).
2) Advanced path: granular controls for traffic selectors, metrics, automatic rollback conditions, and staged percent ramps.
3) Live preview: show simulated traffic slices, estimated QPS distribution, and projected cost delta.
4) Observability hooks: link directly to traces/latency percentiles and quality regression signals (eval set results).
5) Auditability: commit-like view with change owner, timestamp, and one-click revert.
6) Safety autopilot: define fallback policies that trigger based on latency, error-rate, or quality drift, with optional manual approval gates.

Wireframe/flow sketches (annotations):
1) New Rollout Screen (entry)
   - Header: "Create rollout — progressive release"
   - Top row: dropdown to pick route (API key / model route) + current production model snapshot (read-only)
   - Quick-start presets: "Fast canary (default)", "Experiment (A/B)", "Manual staged"
   - Primary action: "Create rollout from preset"; secondary: "Advanced configuration"

2) Preset: Fast canary (default)
   - Steps shown inline: Step 1: 5% for 15m; Step 2: 25% for 30m; Step 3: 100%
   - Each step card includes: ramp %, duration, stop criteria (errors > X, p95 latency > Y, quality delta > Z)
   - Microcopy: "Defaults tuned for minimal user impact. Adjust if your backend accepts cold-starts."

3) Advanced configuration panel (collapsible):
   - Traffic rules: selectors by header, region, API key tag, user cohort; allow regex and hashed bucketing
   - Metric conditions: pick from available signals (p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, eval-score delta) with intuitive operators and recommended thresholds
   - Circuit breaker: toggle with backoff policy (immediate rollback vs step back N% and hold)
   - Canary validation: attach evaluation prompt-set (optional) and set pass threshold (e.g. BLEU/F1/embedding-similarity)
   - Microcopy hints next to each control describing recommended values and cost tradeoffs

4) Preview and simulation
   - Small UI that visualizes traffic timeline and shows estimated QPS through time; simulate with sample workloads (production distribution default)
   - Estimate token-cost delta and latency p95 impact based on the selected model's profile
   - Warning banners if projected capacity exceeds dedicated pool or if quotas may be hit

5) Apply and monitor screen
   - Primary progress timeline with step cards and live indicators (green/yellow/red)
   - Embedded metrics panel with configurable small set of KPIs (latency p95, error rate, eval-quality delta)
   - Quick action buttons: "Pause rollout", "Abort and rollback", "Hold at step", "Increase ramp"
   - Audit trail at bottom: who created, who last modified, linked PR/Jira, timestamps

6) Fallback policy composer (separate modal)
   - Name + scope (route, model group)
   - Trigger types allowed: latency thresholds, error-rate, quality regression vs baseline, missing tokens, KV-cache pressure
   - Response options: fallback to older model, shift to smaller model, redirect to degraded mode (cached responses), throttle new sessions
   - Escalation: notify channel (Slack), create incident ticket, or require manual ACK before rollback

Microcopy suggestions (short snippets to use in UI):
- Next to presets: "Good for typical text-gen models; reduces customer exposure while we validate behavior."
- Metric threshold helper: "Try 2x baseline p95 for latency; start conservative for error-rate."
- Preview tooltip: "Simulation uses last 24h traffic distribution; adjust if you have seasonal variance."
- Rollout banner states: "Paused — awaiting operator action" / "Auto-rolled back due to quality drift"

Operator acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Can create a rollout using the default preset and have it progress automatically with live metric evaluation.
- Ability to define at least one automatic fallback trigger (5xx > 1% sustained for 5m) and a predefined rollback action.
- Preview must show estimated token cost delta and a simple traffic timeline.
- Audit trail entries for create/modify/rollback with timestamps and owner.

Backlog (prioritized):
1) MVP rollout pipeline + default presets + live timeline (P0)
2) Fallback policy modal and wiring to rollout engine (P0)
3) Simulation/preview engine with cost model (P1)
4) Bucketing selectors & regex-based routing (P1)
5) Eval-set attachment and quality-signal plumbing (P1)
6) One-click revert + audit export (P2)
7) Slack/PagerDuty integration for escalation (P2)
8) UX polish: microcopy localization and accessibility review (P2)

Open questions and risks:
- How do we surface model-specific baselines? Need infra to compute and store p95/p99 per model per route.
- Quality signals: which eval metrics become first-class? Embedding-similarity vs task-specific metrics? (ask Applied ML)
- Simulation accuracy: we can estimate cost using per-token stats but latency changes are model/hardware dependent. Add conservative margin.
- Multi-tenant implications for dedicated pools: if rollout will spill across capacity, we need quota checks before applying.

Next steps (short-term owner map):
- Product (Maya): finalize default presets and microcopy; align on acceptance criteria. (Due: 2025-11-21)
- Applied ML (Arjun): propose 2 quality signals and API for attaching eval-sets. (Due: 2025-12-05)
- Serving runtime (Kenji): provide p95/p99 profile export per model and cost estimator hooks. (Due: 2025-12-12)
- Design (Zoe): produce hi-fi wireframes for New Rollout and Apply screens. (Due: 2025-11-28)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally operator-focused: keep defaults conservative. We can iterate on adding more experimental presets.
- Look for missing failure modes (cold-start failures, KV-cache pressure) and add as triggers in fallback composer.

TL;DR: Build a fast-path rollout flow with conservative defaults and a modular fallback policy composer. MVP must include preview simulation, automatic rollback based on simple metrics, and an audit trail. After MVP, iterate on richer routing selectors and eval-linked quality signals.
